Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Vipin Chandra Pandey Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Chandra Shekhar Pandey holding brief of Sri Vipin Chandra Pandey learned counsel for the respondent as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the entire record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 18.08.2023 passed by the Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Agra.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that in this case there is allegation of rape with the victim by the appellant to be committed on 16.06.2023 at about 8 p.m. in the night and F.I.R. was lodged on 18.06.2023 after delay of two days without any explanation thereto.

It is further submitted that as per version in F.I.R. the appellant made the victim fall on the ground and after pressing her mouth snatched her earrings causing injury on her pinna and also committed rape with her.
During medical examination no any injury was found either external or internal on the person of the victim even on the pinna.

It is also submitted that the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. in which she stated that rape was committed with her by the present appellant in association with two other persons namely Khuram Pal and Chotu who caught her hand and legs.

It is also submitted that the victim was literate lady and she herself lodged the F.I.R. but at that time she did not disclose the name of two other persons though F.I.R. was lodged after two days of the alleged incident and again when her statement was recorded before the learned court she added two other persons.
This shows that the present F.I.R. was lodged against the appellant and then after making improvement in her statement also roped two other persons only with ulterior motive.
The statement of sister of the victim herself was recorded by I.O. during the course of investigation in which she did not support the version of the victim.
This shows that the story is totally false and concocted.
The appellant is languishing in jail since 04.08.2023 having no any criminal antecedent.
Learned counsel for the appellant also referred to the amended provisions of SC/ST Act.
All these facts were not taken into consideration by the learned Special Judge while rejecting the bail which cannot be said to be lawful, therefore requested to set it aside and allow the appeal.
Learned counsel for the respondent as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record, the delay in lodging F.I.R. and its version,
the statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and also the statement of her sister, it appears that the learned Special Judge has not taken into consideration all these facts while considering bail,
therefore, the order passed by learned trial court cannot be said to be lawful and is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellant Surajeet Singh @ Bhampu involved in Case Crime No. 154 of 2023 under Sections 376, 506 I.P.C. and 3(2)(V) SC/ST Act, Police Station Fatehabad, District Agra be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.

4. The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5. The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
